title: Annotatio I §.IV (3): Many Lutherans concede tropic speech — Marbachius vs Pezelius
pass_a_gloss: (3.) NOT A FEW LUTHERANS — partly of those who concede the tropic in genus, partly of those who concede either the Metonymic or the Synechdochic in species. From the former we mention Marbachius against Pezelius, p. 36, expressly having allowed that in the proposition This is my body not every figurative locution absolutely is excluded, but only that which forces us to deflect from the proper signification of the several vocables; In which determination of Marbachius the Reformed will easily have rested, urging only tropic locution, not so much its mode, but rather holding promiscuously whether the trope is placed in the words or in the predication.
pass_b_english: (3.) Not a few Lutherans concede tropic speech in genus, or metonymy / synecdoche in species.
Marbachius against Pezelius allows that This is my body does not shut out every figure — only the kind that forces us off each word’s proper signification.
On that the Reformed easily rest, pressing tropic locution while caring less whether the trope sits in the words or in the predication.
source_text: (3.) LUTHERANI NON PAUCI, partim eorum, qui tropicam in genere, eorum partim, qui vel Metonymicam, vel Synechdochicam in specie, concedunt. Ex prioribus memoramus Marbachium contra Pezelium, p. 36. disertis verbis passum, in propositione: Hoc est corpus meum, non in universum omnem figuratam locutionem excludi, sed eam tantùm, quae à propria singularum vocum significatione nos cogit deflectere; In qua Marbachii determinatione facilè acquieverint Reformati, tropicam duntaxat locutionem urgentes, modum ejus non ita, sed promiscuè potiùs habentes, tropus ne in verbis, vel in praedicatione, collocetur.
